<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">the costs under current and future license agreements for our product candidates, including the costs of obtaining and maintaining patent protection for our product candidates,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">the costs of acquiring any technologies or additional product candidates,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">the rate of technological advances,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">the commercial potential of our product candidates,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">the magnitude of our administrative and legal expenses, including office and research development facilities rent, and</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">the costs of establishing third party arrangements for manufacturing.</FONT></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We have incurred negative cash flow from operations since we incorporated and do not expect to generate positive cash flow from our operations for at least the next several years. &nbsp;Therefore, we expect that we will need additional future financings in order to carry out our plan of operations beyond the next twelve months.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We may not be able to obtain adequate financing to fund our operations and any additional financing we obtain may be on terms that are not favorable to us. &nbsp;In addition, any future financings could substantially dilute our stockholders. &nbsp;If adequate funds are not available we will be required to delay, reduce or eliminate one or more of our product development programs, to enter into new collaborative arrangements on terms that are not favorable to us (i.e., the collaborative arrangements could result in the transfer to third parties of rights that we consider valuable), or to cease operations altogether.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We have a limited operating history. &nbsp;We have a large accumulated deficit and may never become profitable.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We have a limited operating history upon which investors may base an evaluation of our likely future performance. &nbsp;Since we began operations in 1999 we have been engaged in developing our research programs, recruiting outside directors and key consultants. &nbsp;We have not generated any revenue to date other than interest income. &nbsp;Our only income other than equity financings has been a modest amount of interest income. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2004, we had an accumulated deficit of $1,232,642<B> </B>and our operating losses are continuing.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We have no products available for sale and we may never be successful in developing products suitable for commercialization.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>All of our product candidates are at an early stage of development and all of our product candidates will require expensive and lengthy testing and regulatory clearances. &nbsp;None of our product candidates have been approved by regulatory authorities. &nbsp;We have no products available for sale and we do not expect to have any products commercially available for several years, if at all. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that our research will lead to the discovery of any commercially viable battery chargers or power generation devices. &nbsp;There are many reasons that we may fail in our efforts to develop our product candidates, including that:</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">our product candidates will be ineffective,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">our product candidates will not be validated by independent testing,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">our product candidates will be too expensive to manufacture or market or will not achieve broad market acceptance,</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">third parties will hold proprietary rights that may preclude us from developing or marketing our product candidates, or</FONT></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt">&bull;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Symbol; font-size:12pt"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">third parties will market equivalent or superior products.</FONT></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We cannot assure you that we will have future revenue or operating profits and you could lose your entire investment.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We expect to incur substantial operating losses for at least the next several years. &nbsp;We currently have sufficient capital resources to fund our operations, with necessary adjustments to our general and administrative budget, at least until March 2006. &nbsp;We currently have no sources revenue and we cannot assure you that we will be able to develop other revenue sources or that our operations will become profitable, even if we are able to commercialize any products. &nbsp;If we do not generate significant increases in revenue, at some point in the future we may not be in a position to continue operations and investors could lose their entire investment.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We do not currently have the capability to undertake manufacturing, marketing, or sales of any potential products.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We have not invested in manufacturing, marketing or product sales resources. &nbsp;We cannot assure you that we will be able to acquire such resources. &nbsp;It is likely that we will also need to hire additional personnel skilled in engineering, product development and manufacturing of components if we develop additional product candidates with commercial potential. &nbsp;We have no history of manufacturing or marketing. &nbsp;We cannot assure you that we will successfully manufacture or market any product we may develop, either independently or under manufacturing or marketing arrangements, if any, with other companies. &nbsp;We currently do not have any arrangements with other companies, and we cannot assure you that any arrangements with other companies can be successfully negotiated or that such arrangements will be on commercially reasonable terms. &nbsp;To the extent that we arrange with other companies to manufacture or market our products, if any, the success of such products may depend on the efforts of those other companies.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>There is considerable technological change and uncertainty in our industry.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We are engaged in the battery charger and energy generation field, which is characterized by extensive research efforts and rapid technological progress. &nbsp;New developments in energy generation devices are expected to continue at a rapid pace in both industry and academia. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that research and discoveries by others will not render some or all of our programs or products noncompetitive or obsolete<B>. &nbsp;</B>Our business strategy is based in large part upon a core technology related to pulse charging of batteries and of capturing back electromagnetic energy and converting this energy into electricity. &nbsp;There is no assurance that the application of these new and unproven technologies will result in the development of commercially viable products for the generation of energy or competitive battery chargers. &nbsp;No assurance can be given that unforeseen problems will not develop with these technologies or applications or we will ultimately develop those commercially feasible products.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We are dependent on executive officers most of whom do not have employment contracts.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Because of the specialized scientific nature of our business, we are highly dependent upon our ability to attract and retain qualified scientific and management personnel. &nbsp;The loss of John Bedini, our Vice President for Research and Development, as well as the licensor of our patent rights would be particularly detrimental to us. &nbsp;Also the loss of any of our other executive officers would be detrimental to us. &nbsp;We do not currently have employment agreements with any of our executive officers. &nbsp;We do not carry key man insurance on any of our personnel.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>There is intense competition for qualified personnel in the areas of our activities, and there can be no assurance that we will be able to continue to attract and retain qualified personnel necessary for the development of our business. &nbsp;Loss of the services of or failure to recruit additional key scientific, technical and management personnel would be detrimental to our research and development programs and business.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Our business could be harmed if we fail to protect our intellectual property.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We have licensed rights to certain patented technology from John Bedini, an officer and director of Energenx, to whom we are obligated to pay royalties if we or our sublicensees develop products based upon the licensed technology. &nbsp;Because of the substantial length of time and expense associated with bringing new products through development and regulatory approval to the marketplace, the battery charger and energy generation industry places considerable importance on patent and trade secret protection for new technologies, products and processes. &nbsp;We have interests in three patents issued in the United States pursuant to our license agreements with John Bedini. &nbsp;We have sublicensed, within North America, certain proprietary technology including our patent rights to two patents to GTG Corp. &nbsp;We are obligated to pay the filing, prosecution and maintenance expenses with regard to all of these patents. &nbsp;We and our licensor plan to file patent applications in other countries, and we may seek additional patents in the future. &nbsp;Our patent position, like that of many technology development companies, is uncertain and involves complex legal and factual questions for which important legal principles are unresolved. &nbsp;We may not develop or obtain rights to products or processes that are patentable. &nbsp;Even if we do obtain additional patents, they may not adequately protect the technology we own or have in-licensed. &nbsp;In addition, others may challenge, seek to invalidate, infringe or circumvent any patents we own or in-license, and rights we receive under those patents may not provide competitive advantages to us. &nbsp;Further, the manufacture, use or sale of our products or processes, if any, may infringe the patent rights of others.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We cannot assure you as to the breadth or the degree of protection that any such patents, if issued, will afford us or that any patents based on the patent applications will be issued at all. &nbsp;In addition, we cannot assure you that others will not independently develop substantially equivalent proprietary information or otherwise obtain access to our know-how or that others may not be issued patents that may require licensing and the payment of significant fees or royalties by us for the pursuit of our business.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Other companies may have filed patent applications or received patents that cover technologies similar to ours. &nbsp;Our ability to make, use or sell any of our product candidates may be blocked by patents that have been or will be issued to third parties that we may not be aware of. &nbsp;The United States patent applications are confidential while pending in the Patent and Trademark Office, and patent applications filed in foreign countries are often first published six months or more after filing. &nbsp;Therefore, until a patent is issued, we have no way of knowing if a third party has a patent that could preclude us from commercializing our product candidates. &nbsp;Third party patent applications and patents could significantly reduce the coverage of our patents and limit our ability to obtain meaningful patent protection. &nbsp;If other companies obtain patents with conflicting claims, we may be required to obtain licenses to these patents or to develop or obtain alternative technology. &nbsp;We may not be able to obtain any such license on acceptable terms or at all. &nbsp;Any failure to obtain such licenses could delay or prevent us from pursuing the development or commercialization of our product candidates, which would adversely affect our business.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Potential litigation concerning patent rights could involve significant expenses and damage our business.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>In the United States, the first to invent a technology is entitled to patent protection on that technology. &nbsp;For patent applications filed prior to January 1, 1996, United States patent law provides that a party who invented a technology outside the United States is deemed to have invented the technology on the earlier of the date it introduced the invention in the United States or the date it filed its patent application. &nbsp;In foreign countries, the first party to file a patent application on a technology, not the first to invent the technology, is entitled to patent protection on that technology. &nbsp;Under the patent laws of most countries, a product can be found to infringe a third party patent if the third party patent expressly covers the product or method of treatment using the product, or if the third party patent covers subject matter that is substantially equivalent in nature to the product or method, even if the patent does not expressly cover the product or method.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>While we have not received notification of potential infringement of patents held by third parties, with respect to any of our product candidates, litigation, patent opposition and adversarial proceedings could result in substantial costs to us. &nbsp;Litigation and/or proceedings could be necessary or may be initiated to enforce any patents we own or in-license, or to determine the scope, validity and enforceability of other parties&#146; proprietary rights and the priority of an invention. &nbsp;The outcome of any of these types of proceedings could significantly affect our product candidates and technology. &nbsp;United States patents carry a presumption of validity and generally can be invalidated only through clear and convincing evidence. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Under our license agreements with John Bedini and with GTG Corp., we have the right to pursue any actions against third parties for infringement of the patent rights covered by those agreements. &nbsp;Under those arrangements we are not obligated to share any recovery from infringement suits brought by us. &nbsp;If we do not bring an infringement action, our licensor or licensee may bring such action and will be entitled to any recovery.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>An adverse outcome of these proceedings could subject us to significant liabilities to third parties, require disputed rights to be licensed from third parties or require us to cease using such technology, any of which could adversely affect our business. &nbsp;Moreover, the mere uncertainty resulting from the initiation and continuation of any technology related litigation or adversarial proceeding could adversely affect our business pending resolution of the disputed matters.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>If we do not exercise our right to prosecute and our licensors institute and prosecute patent proceedings, our rights will depend in part upon the manner in which these licensors conduct the proceedings. &nbsp;In any proceedings they elect to initiate and maintain, these licensors may not vigorously pursue or defend or may decide to settle such proceedings on terms that are unfavorable to us.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Despite the use of confidentiality agreements, which themselves may be of limited effectiveness, it may be difficult for us to protect our trade secrets.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We rely on trade secrets to protect technology in cases when we believe patent protection is not appropriate or obtainable. &nbsp;However, trade secrets are difficult to protect. &nbsp;While we require certain of our corporate collaborators, contractors and consultants to enter into confidentiality agreements, we may not be able to adequately protect our trade secrets or other proprietary information.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We might face intellectual property claims that may be costly to resolve and could divert management attention.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We may from time to time be subject to claims of infringement of other parties&#146; proprietary rights. &nbsp;We could incur substantial costs in defending ourselves in any suits brought against us claiming infringement of the patent rights of others or in asserting our patent rights in a suit against another company. &nbsp;Adverse determinations in any litigation could subject us to significant liabilities to third parties, require us to seek costly licenses from third parties and prevent us or our sublicensees from manufacturing and selling our potential products.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We cannot assure you that our products will be awarded necessary certifications after independent testing.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Our battery charger products will need to be tested independently before they are marketed and sold in the United States by Underwriters Laboratory and other similar organizations in other countries in order to obtain the UL or similar foreign certification product label. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that any products we or our licensees submit for testing of effectiveness and safety by Underwriters Laboratory or similar foreign organization will result in certification of that product. &nbsp;Without such certification sale of the products would be difficult if not impossible.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>If our product candidates do not achieve market acceptance, our business may never achieve profitability.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Our success will depend on the market acceptance of any products we may develop. &nbsp;The degree of market acceptance will depend upon a number of factors, including the receipt and scope of regulatory approvals, the establishment and demonstration in the business community of the safety and effectiveness of our products and their potential advantages over existing technologies. &nbsp;Consumers may not accept or utilize any product that we may develop.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Our controlling stockholders may make decisions that you do not consider to be in your best interest.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>As of March 15, 2005, our directors and executive officers beneficially owned approximately 55%<B> </B>of our outstanding common stock. &nbsp;As a result, our controlling stockholders are able to control all matters requiring stockholder approval, including the election of directors and the approval of significant corporate transactions. &nbsp;This concentration of ownership could also delay or prevent a change in control of Energenx that may be favored by other stockholders.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We are significantly controlled by our management.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Our executive officers comprise three of the six members of the Board of Directors. &nbsp;As a result, our management has the ability to exercise influence over our significant matters. &nbsp;This high level of influence may have a significant effect in delaying, deferring or preventing a change of control of our company.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=center><B>Risks Related to Our Industry</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=center><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Potential technological changes in our field of business create considerable uncertainty.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We are engaged in the battery charger and energy generation field, which is characterized by extensive research efforts and rapid technological progress. &nbsp;New developments in research concerning battery charging and energy generation may occur at a rapid pace in both industry and academia. &nbsp;We cannot assure you that research and discoveries by others will not render some or all of our programs or product candidates noncompetitive or obsolete. &nbsp;We cannot assure you that unforeseen problems will not develop with our technologies or applications or that commercially feasible battery charger or energy generation products will ultimately be developed by us.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>The markets in which we seek to participate are intensely competitive and many of our competitors are better capitalized and have more experience than we do.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>There are many companies, both public and private, including well-known battery manufacturing companies, engaged in developing new types of battery chargers. &nbsp;Our major competitors are currently large companies such as Exide International, Coleman, LVS Sales, Diversified Power International, LLC, EZ-GO, Inc., Lester and Associated. &nbsp;These are large and diversified companies with far ranging capabilities to market their products and to develop follow on products. &nbsp;We are years away from having an energy generation system product ready for the market and we do not currently have the resources to fund the development of such a product through the product development process. &nbsp;In addition we do not have the capability of marketing a battery charger product and will have to enter into a collaborative relationship with a larger company in order to market our battery chargers. &nbsp;It will be difficult to distinguish our battery charger products from the currently battery chargers and gain market share.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Certain smaller battery charger companies may also be competitors, such as Posicharge (a subsidiary of AreoVironment), Japlar Schauer, VDC Electronics, Inc., Deltran, Iota Engineering, Stontronics and Xantrex. &nbsp;Many of these companies have substantially greater capital, research and development and human resources and experience than us and represent significant long-term competition for us. &nbsp;In addition, many of these competitors have significantly greater experience than us in undertaking testing of new products and obtaining regulatory approvals. &nbsp;Furthermore, if we or our current or any future licensee is permitted to commence commercial sales of any product, we or our licensee will also be competing with companies that have greater resources and experience in manufacturing, marketing and sales. &nbsp;We have no experience in these areas. &nbsp;These other companies may succeed in developing products that are more effective or less costly than any that may be developed by us or our future licensee and may also prove to be more successful than us or our future licensee in production and marketing.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>If we successfully develop and obtain approval for our product candidates, we will face competition based on the safety and effectiveness of our products, marketing and sales capability, patent position and other factors. &nbsp;Our competitors may develop or commercialize more effective or more affordable products, or obtain more effective patent protection, than we do. &nbsp;Accordingly, our competitors may commercialize products more rapidly or effectively than we do, which could hurt our competitive position.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>If product liability lawsuits are successfully brought against us, we may incur substantial liabilities and may be required to limit commercialization of our products.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Our business and products will, in the future, expose us to potential product liability risks that in inherent in the testing, manufacturing and marketing of battery chargers and electrical generation products. &nbsp;If we cannot successfully defend ourselves against liability claims, we may incur substantial liabilities or be required to limit commercialization of our products. &nbsp;Our inability to obtain sufficient product liability insurance at an acceptable cost to protect against potential product liability claims could prevent or inhibit the commercialization of products we develop, alone or with corporate collaborators. &nbsp;We do not carry product liability insurance. &nbsp;We may not be able to obtain insurance at a reasonable cost, if at all.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=center><B>Other Risks</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=center><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>There is currently no market for our common stock; if listed the price of our stock may experience considerable volatility.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>There currently is no trading market for our common stock. &nbsp;It is our intention to undertake an initial public offering or engage in another strategy to have our common stock traded on the OTC Bulletin Board under a symbol to be determined. &nbsp;The OTC Bulletin Board is a limited market and subject to substantial restrictions and limitations in comparison to the NASDAQ system. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that a substantial trading market will ever develop for our common stock, or be sustained, if developed, or that current or future shareholders will be able to resell their securities or otherwise liquidate their investment without considerable delay, if at all.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Recent history relating to the market prices of listed newly public companies indicates that, from time to time, there may be significant volatility in the market price of our securities because of factors unrelated, as well as related, to our operating performance. &nbsp;Factors that could have a significant impact on the future market price of our common stock include, but are not limited to, announcements of technological innovations or new products by Energenx or its competitors, government regulatory action, patent or proprietary rights developments and market conditions for companies engaged in the development of alternative energy products. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that our common stock will ever qualify for inclusion within the NASDAQ System, or that more than a limited market will ever develop for our common stock.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>If our common stock is traded at a low price in the future, this may affect the ability of shareholders to sell their shares.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Penny Stock Regulation Broker-dealer practices in connection with transactions in &quot;Penny Stocks&quot; are regulated by certain penny stock rules adopted by the Securities and Exchange Commission. &nbsp;Penny stocks generally are equity securities with a price of less than $5.00 (other than securities registered on certain national securities exchanges or quoted on the NASDAQ system). &nbsp;The penny stock rules require a broker-dealer, prior to a transaction in a penny stock not otherwise exempt from the rules, to deliver a standardized risk disclosure document that provides information about penny stocks and the risk associated with the penny stock market. &nbsp;The broker-dealer must also provide the customer with current bid and offer quotations for the penny stock, the compensation of the broker-dealer and its salesperson in the transaction, and monthly account statements showing the market value of each penny stock held in the customer's account. &nbsp;In addition, the penny stock rules generally require that prior to a transaction in a penny stock, the broker-dealer must make a written determination that the penny stock is a suitable investment for the purchaser and receive the purchaser's written agreement to the transaction. &nbsp;These disclosure requirements may have the effect of reducing the level of trading activity in the secondary market for a stock that becomes subject to the penny stock rules. &nbsp;When and if our common stock is listed on the OTC Bulletin Board, our stock will likely have a trading price of less than $5.00 per share and will not be traded on any exchanges, as they are defined. &nbsp;Therefore, our common stock is likely to become subject to the penny stock rules and investors may find it more difficult to sell their securities, should they desire to do so.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>We do not pay cash dividends.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We have never paid dividends and do not presently intend to pay any dividends in the foreseeable future.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>Item 7.</B></P>
<B><P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Financial Statements.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">The Audited Financial Statements for this Form 10-KSB appear in Item 13 of this annual report, and are hereby incorporated herein by reference.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Item 8.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Changes In and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:45.8pt; font-family:Courier New"><B></B><FONT FACE="Times New Roman">On January 28, 2005, the board of directors of Energenx, Inc. unanimously passed resolutions dismissing the independent accounting firm Beckstead and Watts, LLP, Certified Public Accountants, 3340 Wynn Road, Suite B, Las Vegas, Nevada 89102</FONT> <FONT FACE="Times New Roman">and appointing the independent accounting firm Williams &amp; Webster, PS., Certified Public Accountants, 601 W. Riverside, Suite 1940, Spokane, Washington 99201 to audit the financial statements of Energenx for the year ending December 31, 2004. &nbsp;The board of directors &nbsp;ismissed the accounting firm Beckstead and Watts because that firm had performed the audits for Edward II, Inc., the blank check reporting company that Energenx merged with on December 28, 2004 and was not familiar with the business of Energenx, the surviving corporation.</FONT></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:45.8pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">In its audit of Edward II, Beckstead and Watts had expressed substantial doubt about the ability of Edward II, Inc. the blank check pre-merger corporation, to continue as a going concern because Edward II, Inc. had had limited operations at the time of the audit and had not commenced planned principal operations. &nbsp;Beckstead and Watts' report on the audited financial</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">statements of Edward II did not contain an adverse opinion or a disclaimer of opinion nor was it modified as to uncertainty, audit scope, or accounting principles, except for the going concern paragraph. &nbsp;There were no disagreements at the most recent fiscal year end and any subsequent interim period through the date of dismissal with Beckstead and Watts concerning any matter of accounting principles or practices, financial statement disclosure, or auditing scope or procedure by either Edward II or Energenx. &nbsp;As Energenx was the surviving corporation in the merger transaction the board of directors decided that the independent auditors of the pre-merger corporation Energenx, Williams &amp; Webster, PS., should continue in that capacity.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Item 8A.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Controls and Procedures.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</B>.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Our management, including our Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of our &#147;disclosure controls and procedures&#148; (as such term is defined in Rules 13a-14(c) and 15d-14(c) of the United States Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;)) as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-KSB. &nbsp;Based on that evaluation, our CEO and CFO have concluded that as of end of our last fiscal year, at which time we had just become a reporting company pursuant to Section 13 or 15(d) of the Exchange Act, our disclosure controls and procedures were not sufficiently effective to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in United States Securities and Exchange Commission rules and forms. &nbsp;Material deficiencies were specifically cited in relation to our report on Form 8-K filed on December 30, 2004 concerning our merger/acquisition transaction with a full reporting company, and the manner in which information required to be disclosed therein was summarized and reported in that report under the recently accelerated filing deadlines applicable to Form 8-K reports. &nbsp;As a result of the material deficiencies identified in their evaluation, our CEO and CFO have subsequently put into place disclosure controls and procedures which they believe will provide reasonable assurance that we are enabled to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in United States Securities and Exchange Commission rules and forms.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, does not expect that our disclosure controls and procedures or internal control over financial reporting will prevent all errors and all fraud. &nbsp;A control system, no matter how well conceived and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the system are met and cannot detect all deviations. &nbsp;Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud or deviations, if any, within the company, have been detected. &nbsp;While we believe that our disclosure controls and procedures have been effective, in light of the foregoing, we intend to continue to examine and refine our disclosure control and procedures to monitor ongoing developments in this area.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<BR>
<BR>
<HR style="padding-top:7.2pt; padding-bottom:7.2pt" noshade size=1.333>
<BR>
<BR>
<P style="page-break-before:always; margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=center><B>PART III</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>Item 9.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>Directors and Executive Officers of the Registrant</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>Directors, Executive Officers, Promoters and Control Persons</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>The current executive officers, directors and significant employees of Energenx are as follows:</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B><U>Name</U></B></P>
<B><P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><U>Age</U></B></P>
<B><P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><U>Position</U></B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Gary A. Bedini</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">52</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">President &amp; Chief Executive</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:252pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Officer, Director</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Rick M. Street</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">47</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Chief Financial Officer, Secretary, </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Treasurer, Director</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">John C. Bedini</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">55</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Vice President of Research and,</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Development, Director</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Thomas E. Bearden, Ph.D.</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">76</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Director</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Marvin Redenius</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">40</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Director</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Hans Werner Huss</P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; text-indent:216pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">62</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:288pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">Director</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Each director is elected to hold office for a one year term or until the next annual meeting of stockholders and until his successor is elected and qualified. &nbsp;The officers of Energenx serve at the pleasure of Energenx&#146;s Board of Directors.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>The following sets forth certain biographical information with respect to the directors and executive officers of Energenx.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Gary A. Bedini.</B> &nbsp;Gary Bedini and his brother John Bedini were co-founders of Energenx, previously named Bedini Technology, Inc. &nbsp;Gary Bedini has served as a director and President &amp; CEO of Energenx since September 1999. &nbsp;At the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 18, 2004 Gary Bedini was reelected as a director of Energenx to serve until the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;At a Board Meeting on June 18, 2004, Gary Bedini was reelected as President and Chief Executive Officer of Energenx to serve until the Board of Directors meeting to be held as soon as possible after the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;Mr. Gary Bedini has over 25 years experience in consumer electronics industry. &nbsp;Gary Bedini was a co-founder of Bedini Electronics, Inc. with his brother John Bedini. &nbsp;Mr. Bedini possesses a broad knowledge of procurement, manufacturing, distribution, advertising and sales. &nbsp;Mr. Bedini was instrumental in securing numerous state of the art trade reviews and the 1996 Golden Note Award, given to the most innovative audio products<B>.</B> &nbsp;As a member of H.E.A.A. (Hi End Audio Association) he has participated in numerous efforts to promote and enhance the industries availability into export markets.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Rick M. Street.</B> <B>&nbsp;</B>Rick Street has served as a director of Energenx since November 2001. &nbsp;Mr. Street has served as Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer and Secretary of Energenx since June 2002. &nbsp;At the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 18, 2004 Rick Street was elected as a director of Energenx to serve until the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;At a Board Meeting on June 18, 2004, Rick Street was re-elected as Chief Financial Officer, Treasurer and Secretary of Energenx to serve until the Board of Directors meeting to be held as soon as possible after the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;Rick Street, CPA, CIA has 21 years of management experience in accounting, auditing, development of management information systems, maintaining fully integrated computerized accounting programs designed for small businesses and experienced in all aspects of small business management. &nbsp;From 2002 until present he has been teaching accounting at North Idaho College, Gonzaga University and Spokane Community College. &nbsp;He currently holds a fulltime tenure track position at Spokane Community College and is a principal of an accounting practice in Spokane Washington. &nbsp;From 1996 to 2001 he was the Director of Internal Auditing for the Coeur d&#146;Alene Casino &amp; Resort in Worley, Idaho. &nbsp;From 1991 to 1996, Mr. Street was the controller of the Athletic Round Table, Inc., a non-profit charitable organization. &nbsp;Mr. Street received a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration (accounting) in 1991 from Eastern Washington University and a Masters in Accountancy from Gonzaga University in 2003. &nbsp;He is a Member of the Washington State Society of Certified Public Accountants and a Member of the Institute of Internal Auditors and Chapter Secretary of the Spokane IIA Chapter.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>John C. Bedini.</B> &nbsp;John Bedini and his brother Gary Bedini were co-founders of Energenx, previously named Bedini Technology, Inc. &nbsp;John Bedini has been a director, Vice President of Energenx since September 1999. &nbsp;At the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 18, 2004 John Bedini was re-elected as a director of Energenx to serve until the 2003 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;At a Board Meeting on June 18, 2004, John Bedini was reelected as Vice President for Research and Development of Energenx to serve until the Board of Directors meeting to be held as soon as possible after the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;Mr. John Bedini is a scientist and well-known inventor. &nbsp;His work has produced many innovative audio products that have been marketed over a 25-year period to the audio electronics industry. &nbsp;Mr. Bedini has also developed a variety of products and technically innovative products for several different industries. &nbsp;His inventions include the BEDINI line of audio amplifiers, Bedini Audio Spacial Environment (B.A.S.E.), the Bedini Clarifier products, the Binaural Audio and several instruments for the medical industry. &nbsp;He has been awarded many patents related to his various inventions. &nbsp;Mr. Bedini has received broad industry recognition including designation as Distinguished Scientist of the year by the Association of Distinguished American Scientists. &nbsp;He is a graduate of Bell and Howell Institute of Technology. </P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Thomas E. Bearden, Ph.D.</B> &nbsp;Thomas Bearden has served as a director of Energenx since June 2001. &nbsp;At the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 18, 2004 Mr. Bearden was reelected as a director of Energenx to serve until the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders.<B> &nbsp;</B>Thomas Bearden is a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of Energenx. &nbsp;Tom Bearden is a research scientist, inventor, consultant, and holds Ph.D. (Trinity University) in Science, M.S. (Georgia Tech) in Nuclear Engineering, and B.S. (Northeast Louisiana State) in mathematics. &nbsp;has participated in founding the first legitimate theory of COP&gt;1.0 EM systems published in leading scientific journals. &nbsp;Dr. Bearden is Director of the Association of Distinguished American Scientists (ADAS), a Fellow Emeritus of the Alpha Foundation's Institute for Advanced Study (AIAS), CEO of CTEC, Inc., a private research and development company based in Huntsville, Alabama and serves as a member on the board of directors of two private companies. &nbsp;He has authored or co-authored more than 200 professional papers in the literature and has published several technical books. &nbsp;In his work with the AIAS, he has participated in authoring and co-authoring more than 100 scientific papers primarily in the area of advanced electrodynamics. &nbsp;Approximately one third of the papers have been published in leading scientific and research journals. &nbsp;Of the published articles one half of them are related to extracting usable electromagnetic energy.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Marvin Redenius.</B> &nbsp;Marvin Redenius has served as a director of Energenx since his appointment to the board in March 2004<B>.</B> to serve until the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;At the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 18, 2004 Mr. Redenius was reelected as a director of Energenx to serve until the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders.<B> &nbsp;</B>Since 1990, Mr. Redenius has been the owner of Farm Advantage, Inc., an agriculture supply company operating in the mid-western U.S. &nbsp;Farm Advantage supplies innovative agricultural products and services. &nbsp;The company warehouses and distributes products from North Central, Iowa and has annual sales in excess of 40 million dollars. &nbsp;Mr. Redenius also owns and operates Northern National Trucking, Inc., which consists of a fleet of 30 tractor trailers. &nbsp;Mr. Redenius and his family also own and operate Cristina Corp, a farm corporation. &nbsp;Mr. Redenius also owns GTG Corporation, which invests in early stage technology based companies. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Hans Werner Huss.</B> &nbsp;Hans Werner Huss has served as a director of Energenx since January 2002. &nbsp;At the 2004 Annual Meeting of Stockholders held on June 18, 2004 Mr. Huss was reelected as a director of Energenx to serve until the 2005 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. &nbsp;Mr. Huss graduated Diplom Ingenieur Electrical Engineering, with emphasis on Electronics, from the Technical University in Munich, Germany. &nbsp;He currently serves as President and Chairman of a new technology company Integrated Micrometallurgical Systems, Inc. based in Spokane, Washington. &nbsp;He is also involved in Consulting for several other start-up companies with promising new technologies, advising them in business and marketing matters. &nbsp;Previously, he has served in many functions in different companies in the U.S. and in Europe, most notably in executive positions of several high tech companies in different industries, such as: President, Euromissile G.I.E. in Paris, France (a management and sales company for missile systems in the EADS Group &#150; European Aeronautics Defense and Space Company); President, MEADS International, Inc., in Orlando/Florida (tri-national management company for the Medium Extended Air Defense System, under contract from NAMEADSMA, the NATO agency in Huntsville, AL, managing this tri-national system under joint development in the U.S., Germany, and Italy); President, Magnetic Transit of America, Inc., in Los Angeles, CA (engineering and marketing company for a Mag-Lev Transportation system for inner urban use; a subsidiary of AEG/Daimler-Benz); General Manager of IBCOL Technical Services GmbH, in Munich, Germany (internationally operating marketing and sales company mainly in the fields of aircraft, aircraft parts, transportation systems, security and surveillance systems, medical systems); and, Program Manager for a mobile air defense system at Euromissile, Paris, France and at MBB, Munich, Germany.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Gary A. Bedini is the brother of John C. Bedini. &nbsp;There are no other family relationships between any of the officers and directors.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>As we are a development stage company with no revenues from operations, few employees, and relatively simple financial statements, we have not, at this stage, constituted any board committees, including an audit committee. &nbsp;We intend to do so in the near future. &nbsp;Consequently we do not have an audit committee financial expert who is an outside director. &nbsp;As our business grows and our financial statements become more complicated, we intend to seek an outside director who can qualify as an audit committee financial expert.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We have not adopted a code of ethics that applies to our President and CEO (principal executive officer), or our Chief Financial Officer (principal accounting officer). &nbsp;As we have just recently become a reporting company required to file periodic reports with the SEC and as our common stock is not currently listed on any exchange, we have not yet dealt with this issue, but we intend to do so in the near future.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:36pt; text-indent:-36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><B>Section 16(a) Beneficial Ownership Reporting Compliance.</B></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Initial reports on Form 3 filed on behalf of each of Gary A. Bedini, President and Chief Executive Officer, Rick M. Street, Chief Financial Officer, Secretary and Treasurer, John C. Bedini, Vice President for Research and Development, Thomas E. Bearden, Director, Hans Werner Huss, Director and Marvin Redenius, Director, were filed late concerning the acquisition and merger transaction on December 27, 2004 pursuant to which Energenx became a reporting company.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:-14pt; padding-left:72pt; text-indent:-72pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt"><B>Item 10.</B></P>

<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt">There were no option grants to our Named Executive Officer in 2004. &nbsp;No option grants have been made to any of our executive officers under the Energenx 1999 Stock Option Plan to date. &nbsp;We have not granted any stock appreciation rights.</P>

<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>Energenx does not have an employment contract with its Named Executive Officer or any of its executive officers.</P>
<P style="margin:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="margin:0pt; text-indent:36pt; line-height:14pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:12pt" align=justify>We do not have any arrangements with our Named Executive Officer or any of our other executive officers triggered by termination of employment or change in control.</P>
